claims.claim: In certain heterogeneous network models, random node failures and targeted removal of important hubs produce different connectivity responses.
claims.locator: Albert, Jeong and Barabási (2000), Nature abstract and network comparison

claims.claim: The original Nature article has a published correction concerning particular measurements/figures; the described attack-response conclusions should be attributed to the corrected record.
claims.locator: Correction: Error and attack tolerance of complex networks

claims.claim: Random breakdown percolation for network degree distributions is distinct from deliberate high-degree attacks.
claims.locator: Cohen et al. (2000), random breakdown analysis

claims.claim: Intentional high-degree attacks require a different removal protocol and can be analyzed using intentional breakdown methods.
claims.locator: Cohen et al. (2001), targeted removal framework

claims.claim: Load redistribution after a failure can trigger additional overload failures; this dynamic mechanism differs from static connectivity loss.
claims.locator: Motter and Lai (2002), Cascade-based attacks on complex networks

claims.claim: Deleting star hub 0 versus leaf 6 gives 1/6 versus 1 in surviving-node LCC fraction; path center gives 3/6.
claims.locator: Derived from star_graph(6), path_graph(7) and independently checked connected components

claims.claim: If one failed server load of 4 is split equally onto two servers initially at load 4, new load is 6 and additional failure count depends on whether capacity is 5 or 6.
claims.locator: Illustrative one-round redistribution toy, explicitly not reproducing the Motter–Lai model
